title: Academic Rules 2025
content: CHITKARA UNIVERSITY Office of Academic Affairs CU/ACAD/ORD/2025-26 Uncontrolled copy when printed Page 1 Academic Ordinances & Rules Governing regulations for attendance, evaluation, grading and branch change eligibility — Undergraduate Programmes Document Code CU/ACAD/ORD/2025-26 Applicable To All UG students, Batches 2022–2026 through 2025–2029 Effective From 01 August 2025 Approved By Academic Council, Chitkara University Version 3.1 (Supersedes v3.0 dated 12 Jan 2025)

title: Academic Rules 2025
content: 1. Mandatory Attendance Requirement 1.1 Every student must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance in each registered course (theory, laboratory, tutorial, and studio components counted separately) calculated cumulatively from the first working day of the semester up to the last instructional day. 1.2 Attendance is recorded on a per-lecture / per-session basis through the Learning Management System (LMS) and is visible to students in real time on the Student Portal under "My Attendance." 1.3 A student whose attendance falls below 75% in any course at the end of the semester is detained from appearing in the End Semester Examination (ESE) for that course and is awarded a grade of "DT" (Detained) on the grade card. 1.4 Students detained under Clause 1.3 must re-register for and repeat the course (along with attendance and internal assessment) the next time it is offered. 1.5 Medical / Documented Exemption A relaxation of up to 10% on the mandatory attendance requirement (i.e., a floor of 65%) may be granted by the Dean of Academic Affairs on the recommendation of the Head of Department, only where all of the following conditions are satisfied:  The absence is supported by a certificate from a registered medical practitioner or government hospital, submitted within 7 working days of resuming classes.  The absence does not exceed 15 consecutive instructional days in a single spell, except in cases of hospitalisation, which require the discharge summary as additional proof.  A duly filled Attendance Exemption Form (Form AA-04), countersigned by the parent/guardian and the class coordinator, is submitted to the Department Office.  The exemption request is filed before the last teaching day of the semester; retrospective requests after result declaration are not entertained. Note: The 10% medical relaxation reduces the effective requirement to 65%; it does not waive attendance altogether. Sports, NCC/NSS, and university-representation duty are covered under a separate Duty Leave provision (Clause 1.6) and are recorded as "present" for attendance computation, subject to prior approval from the Dean of Student Welfare. 1.6 Duty Leave Students representing the University in inter-university sports, technical festivals, cultural competitions, NCC/NSS camps, or academic conferences (with a presented/accepted paper) may avail Duty Leave on submission of Form AA-07 at least 3 working days in advance, endorsed by the concerned Dean/Director. Duty Leave days are counted as present but are capped at 15 working days per semester per student.

title: Academic Rules 2025
content: 2. Grading Scale The University follows a 10-point Relative Grading System. Final grades in each course are computed from a weighted combination of Continuous Internal Assessment (CIA) and the End Semester Examination, in the ratio notified by the concerned School at the start of the semester (typically 40:60 for theory and 50:50 for lab-heavy courses). Grade Marks Range (%) Grade Point Description O 90 – 100 10 Outstanding A+ 80 – 89 9 Excellent A 70 – 79 8 Very Good B+ 60 – 69 7 Good B 55 – 59 6 Above Average C 50 – 54 5 Average P 40 – 49 4 Pass F Below 40 0 Fail — reappear required DT — 0 Detained (attendance shortfall) I — — Incomplete (pending result / audit) 2.1 Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) is computed as the credit-weighted average of grade points across all courses completed up to the current semester. Semester Grade Point Average (SGPA) covers a single semester only. 2.2 A minimum grade of "P" (Grade Point 4) is required to clear a course. A grade of "F" requires the student to reappear in the ESE (backlog) in the immediately following exam cycle, or re-register for the full course if two consecutive reappear attempts are unsuccessful. 2.3 Grade cards are issued through the Student Portal within 21 working days of the last ESE paper of the semester. Physical grade cards are issued only at the end of the programme.

title: Academic Rules 2025
content: 3. Branch Change Eligibility Students seeking a change of branch/specialisation after the first year of the programme must satisfy all of the following criteria:  Minimum CGPA of 8.50 at the end of the Second Semester, computed on all courses attempted (including electives and audit courses carrying credit).  No active backlog — no course with grade "F" or "DT" pending clearance at the time of application.  Availability of a vacant seat in the target branch, subject to the sanctioned intake approved by the University and applicable regulatory body for that academic year.  Submission of the Branch Change Application (Form AA-11) within the notified window, typically the first two weeks of the Third Semester. 3.1 Where the number of eligible applicants for a target branch exceeds available seats, selection is made strictly in order of CGPA, with ties resolved by the Second Semester SGPA, and thereafter by the First Semester SGPA.

title: Academic Rules 2025
content: CHITKARA UNIVERSITY Office of Academic Affairs CU/ACAD/ORD/2025-26 Uncontrolled copy when printed Page 3 3.2 A branch change once granted and confirmed is final for the duration of the programme. Fee structure applicable to the new branch (if different) takes effect from the semester of transfer; no retrospective fee adjustment is made for prior semesters.

title: Academic Rules 2025
content: 4. Unfair Means & Academic Integrity — Cross-Reference Provisions relating to use of unfair means during examinations, plagiarism in assignments/reports, and associated penalties are governed separately under the Examination Regulations document (CU/ACAD/EXAM/2025-26); this document addresses attendance, grading and branch-change matters only. This document is issued for general student guidance. In case of any conflict between this summary and the full Academic Ordinances approved by the Academic Council, the version held by the Office of Academic Affairs shall prevail. Queries: academics@chitkara.edu.in

title: Central Library Rules
content: 1. Membership & Access 1.1 Every registered student is automatically enrolled as a Library member using their University ID card, which doubles as the library card; a separate library card is not issued. 1.2 Entry to the Library requires the ID card to be tapped at the turnstile; bags, food, and beverages are not permitted beyond the entrance lockers, except transparent water bottles.

title: Central Library Rules
content: 2. Borrowing Limits & Loan Period Member Category Books Allowed Loan Period UG Students 4 books 14 days PG Students 6 books 14 days Research Scholars (PhD/MPhil) 8 books 30 days Faculty Members 10 books One semester Reference / Reserved-section titles Not for home loan Reading room use only 2.1 An Undergraduate student may borrow up to 4 books at a time for a loan period of 14 days, renewable once for a further 14 days provided no other member has placed a hold/reservation on the title. 2.2 Renewal may be done in person at the Circulation Desk or online through the Library Portal (OPAC) up to 2 days before the due date; books already overdue are not eligible for online renewal and must be returned/renewed physically after fine clearance. 2.3 Textbooks placed in the "High Demand / Semester Reserve" shelf carry a shorter loan period of 3 days (overnight issue after 5:00 PM, return by 10:00 AM next day) to ensure equitable access during examinations.

Reading Room Timings Period Timing Regular semester (Mon–Sat) 8:00 AM – 10:00 PM Sundays & Gazetted holidays 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM Examination period (extended hours) 7:00 AM – 12:00 Midnight, all days Circulation (borrow/return) counter 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM, Mon–Sat Vacation / semester break 10:00 AM – 5:00 PM, Mon–Fri only 4.1 During the extended examination-period hours, the Reading Room remains staffed by a duty librarian and security personnel; students must carry their ID card at all times inside the premises. 4.2 Silence zones are strictly enforced in the Reading Room and Reference section; group discussion is permitted only in the designated Discussion Rooms, bookable in advance through the Library Portal.

title: Central Library Rules
content: 5. General Conduct in the Library  Marking, highlighting, or removing pages from Library material is treated as damage and billed at replacement cost.  Mobile phones must be kept on silent mode; calls must be taken outside the Reading Room.  Personal books/bags left unattended on reading tables beyond 30 minutes may be moved to the custody desk to free up seating during peak hours.  Inter-library loan (ILL) requests for titles not held in the Central Library collection may be raised through the Librarian and are subject to the lending institution's terms. This document summarises Library rules for general member guidance and complements the digital Library Catalogue (OPAC). For the complete Library Manual, contact the Circulation Desk. title: Exam Regulations
content: CHITKARA UNIVERSITY Office of Academic Affairs CU/ACAD/EXAM/2025-26 Uncontrolled copy when printed Page 1 Examination Regulations Unfair means, seating arrangements, and minimum passing criteria — All Semester Examinations Document Code CU/ACAD/EXAM/2025-26 Applicable To All UG & PG students appearing in CIA/Mid-Term and End Semester Examinations Effective From 01 August 2025 Approved By Controller of Examinations Version 2.3

title: Exam Regulations
content: 1. Seating Arrangement 1.1 Seating for the End Semester Examination is allotted centrally by the Examination Cell and published on the Student Portal and examination hall notice boards at least 3 days before the first paper.  Students are seated by roll number in a zig-zag / alternate pattern across rows, with a minimum gap of one vacant seat on either side wherever hall capacity permits.  Where two examinations are held simultaneously in adjoining halls, different courses/subjects are interleaved row-wise to minimise the possibility of copying between adjacent candidates.  A student must occupy only the seat number printed on their admit card; occupying another seat without permission from the Room Superintendent is itself recorded as an irregularity.  Bags, books, notes, and mobile phones must be deposited at the front of the hall before the exam begins; only admit card, ID card, and permitted stationery are allowed at the desk. 1.2 Entry to the examination hall closes 15 minutes after commencement of the paper; no candidate is permitted entry thereafter, and no candidate is permitted to leave within the first 30 minutes or the last 10 minutes of the examination.

title: Exam Regulations
content: 2. Use of Unfair Means (UFM) 2.1 "Unfair means" includes, without limitation: possession of unauthorised material (written notes, programmed devices, mobile phones) in the examination hall; copying from another candidate or allowing one's own answer script to be copied; impersonation; disorderly conduct towards invigilation staff; and any act calculated to secure an unfair advantage in an examination or continuous assessment (including plagiarism in project reports/assignments). 2.2 An invigilator detecting a suspected UFM case must seize the material/device, record a written report co-signed by the candidate (or noting refusal to sign), and forward the answer script and evidence to the Controller of Examinations the same day. The candidate is permitted to complete the remainder of the examination under observation, without prejudice to the outcome of the enquiry. 2.3 Penalty Structure Category Nature of Offence Penalty Category A Possession of chits/notes (unused), unauthorised stationery Cancellation of that paper; grade "UM" for the course Category B Copying from another candidate / mutual copying; use of mobile phone or programmed device Cancellation of all papers of that semester examination Category C Impersonation, use of forged admit card, or misconduct towards invigilation staff Cancellation of examination for 2 consecutive semesters; disciplinary referral Category D Leakage/circulation of question paper, or repeat offence under Category B/C Rustication from the University for a period determined by the Disciplinary Committee (minimum one academic year)

title: Exam Regulations
content: CHITKARA UNIVERSITY Office of Academic Affairs CU/ACAD/EXAM/2025-26 Uncontrolled copy when printed Page 2 2.4 All UFM cases are heard by the Unfair Means Committee, which affords the candidate an opportunity to be heard before a penalty is confirmed. A candidate found using unfair means loses the right to "benefit of doubt" grading and, for Category B and above, is also debarred from being considered for scholarships/merit awards for the academic year in question. 2.5 A candidate may appeal the Committee's decision in writing to the Controller of Examinations within 7 working days of communication of the penalty; the appeal is placed before an Appellate Committee whose decision is final.

title: Exam Regulations
content: CHITKARA UNIVERSITY Office of Academic Affairs CU/ACAD/EXAM/2025-26 Uncontrolled copy when printed Page 3

title: Exam Regulations
content: 3. Minimum Passing Marks 3.1 To clear a course, a candidate must secure:  A minimum of 40% aggregate marks (Continuous Internal Assessment + End Semester Examination combined), corresponding to Grade "P" or above, and  A minimum of 30% marks in the End Semester Examination component alone, even where the combined aggregate crosses 40% — a candidate scoring below this ESE floor is awarded grade "F" irrespective of internal marks.  For laboratory/practical courses, a separate minimum of 40% in the practical/viva-voce component is required in addition to the theory component, where the course carries both. 3.2 There is no separate minimum threshold within Continuous Internal Assessment alone; however, a candidate scoring zero in CIA due to non-submission of assignments or non-appearance in a Mid-Term test is not exempted from the ESE floor above. 3.3 Candidates who fail to meet the criteria in Clause 3.1 are classified as having grade "F" and must reappear in the ESE for that course in the next available examination cycle (backlog/reappear), on payment of the prescribed reappear fee.

title: Exam Regulations
content: 4. Re-evaluation & Rechecking 4.1 A candidate may apply for rechecking (verification of totalling and ensuring all answers are evaluated) within 10 days of result declaration; revaluation (re-assessment by a second examiner) is permitted only for theory papers, not for practicals, vivas, or CIA components, and is subject to the fee notified in the Fee Circular. 4.2 Where revaluation results in a change of 10% or more in the marks originally awarded, the revaluation fee is refunded to the candidate. This document summarises the Examination Regulations for general student awareness. The detailed Unfair Means enquiry procedure and the full Examination Manual are maintained by the Examination Cell. Queries: examcell@chitkara.edu.in

content: CHITKARA UNIVERSITY Office of Academic Affairs CU/FIN/CIRC/EVEN-2026 Uncontrolled copy when printed Page 1 Fee Deadlines & Scholarships Circular Even Semester — Tuition fee schedule, late fee penalties, exam fee and refund policy Document Code CU/FIN/CIRC/EVEN-2026 Applicable To All UG & PG students enrolled for the Even Semester (Jan–Jun 2026) Effective From 01 January 2026 Issued By Office of the Finance Controller Version 2.0

title: Fee Circular Even Sem
content: 1. Tuition Fee Payment Schedule 1.1 Tuition fee for the Even Semester is payable in a single instalment through the Student Portal (Payment Gateway: HDFC / Net Banking / UPI) or via Demand Draft favouring "Chitkara University" payable at Rajpura. Milestone Date Applicable Fine Fee due date (no penalty) 26 March 2026 Nil Late payment window 1 27 Mar – 09 Apr 2026 ■500 flat fine Late payment window 2 10 Apr – 23 Apr 2026 ■1,500 flat fine Final cut-off with Dean's approval 24 Apr – 07 May 2026 ■3,000 fine + written undertaking After 07 May 2026 — Name struck off rolls; re-admission fee applies 1.2 A fine of ■500 is levied automatically for payments made after 26 March 2026; this is the standard late fee referenced across University communication. Fines in Windows 2 and 3 above are cumulative escalations for prolonged non-payment and are not routinely waived. 1.3 Students on an approved education loan must submit the bank sanction letter to the Finance Office before the due date to obtain a provisional payment extension of up to 30 days; the fine schedule above is suspended only for the loan-disbursed portion of the fee. 1.4 Fee instalment plans (2 or 3 part payment) are available only to students who applied and were approved in the Odd Semester of the same academic year; new instalment requests cannot be raised mid-way through the Even Semester.

title: Fee Circular Even Sem
content: 2. Examination Fee 2.1 Examination fee for the End Semester Examination is billed separately from tuition and must be cleared at least 10 days before the commencement of the exam schedule; a student with an outstanding exam fee is not issued an admit card / hall ticket. title: Fee Circular Even Sem
content: 3. Scholarships 3.1 Merit and merit-cum-means scholarships are disbursed as a fee waiver credited directly against the tuition ledger before the due date, provided eligibility documents (previous semester grade card, income certificate where applicable) are uploaded on the Scholarship Portal by 15 February 2026.  Merit Scholarship: Students securing CGPA 9.0 and above in the preceding semester — up to 25% tuition waiver, renewed automatically each semester subject to maintaining CGPA 8.5+.  Sports/Cultural Scholarship: State/National level achievers — waiver ranging 10%–50% as assessed by the Sports Committee, valid for the academic year.  Means-cum-Merit Scholarship: Family income below ■6,00,000 p.a. with CGPA 7.5+ — waiver assessed case-by-case by the Financial Aid Committee.  Sibling/Alumni Concession: 10% concession on tuition where a sibling is concurrently enrolled, or the applicant is a child of a Chitkara University alumnus (proof required). 3.2 Scholarships are not cumulative beyond a combined ceiling of 50% of tuition fee unless specifically approved by the Vice-Chancellor's office. A scholarship is forfeited for the following semester if the student incurs a backlog ("F" grade) or a disciplinary sanction.

title: Fee Circular Even Sem
content: 4. Refund Policy Point of Withdrawal Refundable Amount Before commencement of classes 100% of fee, less ■1,000 processing charge Within 15 days of commencement 90% of semester tuition fee 16 – 30 days of commencement 50% of semester tuition fee After 30 days of commencement No refund of tuition fee Caution money / security deposit Refundable on clearance, minus dues, after final exit 4.1 Refunds are processed only to the original mode of payment / the fee-payer's bank account on record, within 15–21 working days of the No-Dues Certificate being cleared by the Finance Office, Library, Hostel (if applicable), and concerned Department. 4.2 Hostel fee and mess fee refunds are governed separately under the Hostel & Campus Life Rulebook and are pro-rated by the number of days of actual occupancy in the month of withdrawal. Figures in this circular are illustrative of the Even Semester 2026 cycle and are revised annually by the Finance Committee. For the fee schedule of a specific programme/batch, check the "Fee Structure" tab on the Student Portal. Queries: fees.helpdesk@chitkara.edu.in

title: Hostel Guidelines
content: CHITKARA UNIVERSITY Office of Academic Affairs CU/HOS/RULE/2025-26 Uncontrolled copy when printed Page 1 Hostel & Campus Life Rulebook Curfew timings, anti-ragging policy, visitor rules and mess schedule — Resident Students Document Code CU/HOS/RULE/2025-26 Applicable To All students residing in University hostels (Boys' & Girls' Blocks) Effective From 01 July 2025 Issued By Office of the Dean, Student Welfare / Chief Warden Version 4.2

title: Hostel Guidelines
content: 1. Curfew & In-Time Regulations Category In-Time (Mon–Sat) In-Time (Sun / Holiday) UG Students (1st & 2nd Year) 8:30 PM 8:00 PM UG Students (3rd Year & above) 9:30 PM 9:00 PM PG / Research Scholars 10:00 PM 9:30 PM Late entry (prior gate-pass approved) Up to 10:30 PM Up to 10:00 PM 1.1 The standard in-time (curfew) for general UG residents from the Third Year onward is 9:30 PM on working days, recorded via biometric attendance at the hostel main gate. First and second year residents observe an earlier in-time of 8:30 PM in line with the Anti-Ragging and student-safety protocol for new entrants. 1.2 Three unexplained late entries in a semester result in a written warning; a fourth instance is referred to the Hostel Disciplinary Committee and may attract a fine of ■500 per instance thereafter or a period of early curfew (7:30 PM) for the remainder of the semester. 1.3 Overnight leave (Out-Pass) beyond curfew requires prior written consent from a parent/guardian submitted through the Hostel Portal at least 12 hours in advance, and is capped at 4 occasions per month.

title: Hostel Guidelines
content: 2. Anti-Ragging Policy 2.1 Chitkara University maintains a strict zero-tolerance policy on ragging in accordance with UGC Regulations, 2009 and applicable state Anti-Ragging Acts, across hostel premises, mess halls, common rooms, and campus grounds.  All fresh entrants and their parents/guardians must submit a signed Anti-Ragging Affidavit (online, via the UGC Anti-Ragging portal and the University portal) before hostel allotment.  Anti-Ragging Squads conduct surprise checks in hostel corridors, mess, and common areas, particularly during the first 90 days of an academic year.  A 24x7 Anti-Ragging Helpline and a designated Anti-Ragging Committee (chaired by the Dean, Student Welfare) are constituted to receive and act on complaints confidentially.  Confirmed incidents of ragging attract penalties ranging from a written apology and fine, up to rustication, expulsion from the hostel, debarment from examinations, or expulsion from the University, as per the severity assessed by the Committee, without prejudice to criminal proceedings under law. 2.2 Any student witnessing or experiencing ragging is encouraged to report immediately to the Warden-on-Duty, the Anti-Ragging Helpline, or anonymously through the drop-box installed in each hostel block. Retaliation against a complainant is treated as a separate, aggravated offence.

title: Hostel Guidelines
content: CHITKARA UNIVERSITY Office of Academic Affairs CU/HOS/RULE/2025-26 Uncontrolled copy when printed Page 2

title: Hostel Guidelines
content: 3. Visitor & Guest Rules 3.1 Visitors (parents/guardians and University-approved guests) are permitted only in the designated Visitors' Lounge at the hostel entrance, between 10:00 AM and 6:00 PM on all days; visitors are not permitted inside residential wings under any circumstance. 3.2 Every visitor must register at the security gate with a valid photo ID; the resident student is intimated and must personally receive the visitor at the lounge. 3.3 Opposite-gender visitors, including family members, are restricted to the Visitors' Lounge only and are not permitted in the hostel premises beyond the reception/lounge area at any time. 3.4 Overnight stay of guests inside student rooms is strictly prohibited. Parents requiring overnight accommodation may be directed to the University Guest House, subject to availability and prior booking.

title: Hostel Guidelines
content: 4. Mess Timings & Rules Meal Timing (Mon–Sun) Breakfast 7:00 AM – 9:00 AM Lunch 12:30 PM – 2:15 PM Evening Tea/Snacks 5:00 PM – 6:00 PM Dinner 7:30 PM – 9:15 PM Night canteen (paid, optional) 9:30 PM – 11:30 PM 4.1 Mess attendance is via biometric/ID card tap at entry; students on approved medical leave or an out-pass may claim a pro-rated mess fee rebate for absences of 5 or more consecutive days, applied for through Form HW-02 within 7 days of resuming. 4.2 A rotating weekly menu, including at least one special meal on Sunday, is displayed on the mess notice board and the Hostel Portal; dietary requests (medical/religious) are coordinated through the Mess Committee representative of each block.

title: Hostel Guidelines
content: 5. General Conduct  Possession or consumption of alcohol, tobacco, or any prohibited substance within hostel premises is strictly prohibited and treated as major misconduct.  Use of electric heaters, induction cooktops, or open-flame appliances in rooms is prohibited on fire-safety grounds; violation attracts confiscation and a fine.  Loud music/noise after 10:30 PM ("quiet hours") is not permitted in consideration of fellow residents, especially during examination periods.  Room changes/reallotments are handled only by the Warden's Office at the start of a semester; informal swaps between students are not recognised for record purposes. This rulebook is a general summary for resident-student guidance and campus orientation; the complete Hostel Manual with detailed disciplinary procedure is available with the respective Warden's Office. Anti-Ragging Helpline (24x7): 1800-XXX-XXXX. Queries: hostel.warden@chitkara.edu.in
